_readme: Global game values. Edit, save, then press T in the running game (or restart it). Keys starting with _ are notes. Leave a key out to use its default from scripts/core/tuning.gd.

rules._notes: Changing these changes every puzzle. Re-check the levels after a change: python3 tools/sim.py levels/*.json

loop._notes: The belt never stops while cubes ride it. Speed is along the belt in screen pixels per second (the screen is 1080 wide; the loops are 2500 to 3900 px around). The gap spaces out cubes that left a tray together, when jelly rides in cups.

feedback._notes: The tray wobble when a tap can't send anything (no free cups).

goo._notes: The flowing jelly on the belt. The rules still place every cube; this is only how it looks and moves. enabled false rides jelly in cups instead. One cube's goo covers one belt space (the belt's length divided by the level's cups), so a full belt is covered end to end; belt_fill under 1 leaves gaps (0.8 covers 80% when full). A cube is a line of soft gobs gob_spacing_px apart, each drawn as a blob of blob_radius_px that melts into its neighbors. cling is how hard a flavor holds together, slosh how far it swings out on bends, jostle how restless it is (0 is still). Battery: wider gob_spacing_px (fewer gobs), and lower field_scale and render_scale (the goo is drawn small, then smoothed up to screen size), all cost less.

solver._notes: A testing readout under the board that says whether the board can still be finished. It never stops the game: the game stops only when every cup is full and no cube can land. Turn it off to play blind.

look._notes: Sizes in screen pixels (the screen is 1080 x 2340); colors as hex. Cube size must stay under 76 (the tray cavity). Jelly sprites are white and take their color from flavors, so palette changes need no new art. jelly_gloss scales the shine on jelly.
